item.description:
884
ACPN50 PHFO 252309

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Sun Oct 25 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on recently
downgraded Tropical Storm Vance, located a few hundred miles
west-southwest of Acapulco, Mexico, and on recently upgraded
Tropical Storm Olana, located several hundred miles west-southwest
of Johnston Atoll.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Olana are issued under
WMO header WTPA33 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCPCP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Olana are issued under
WMO header WTPA23 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCMCP3.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Cangialosi

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Olana (CP3/CP032026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...OLANA HOLDING STEADY WHILE MOVING EAST-NORTHEASTWARD... As of 5:00 PM HST Sun Oct 25 the center of Olana was located near 14.9, -177.3 with movement ENE at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1002 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 40 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Olana Public Advisory Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sun Oct 25 2026 
296 
WTPA33 PHFO 260231
TCPCP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Olana Advisory Number   3
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP032026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Sun Oct 25 2026
 
...OLANA HOLDING STEADY WHILE MOVING EAST-NORTHEASTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.9N 177.3W
ABOUT 535 MI...860 KM WSW OF JOHNSTON ISLAND
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...ENE OR 75 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in Johnston Atoll should monitor the progress of this
system.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Olana was
located near latitude 14.9 North, longitude 177.3 West. Olana is
moving toward the east-northeast near 9 mph (15 km/h) and a general
eastward motion is expected during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Some slight strengthening is possible tonight, but weakening 
is forecast to begin on Monday. Olana is now forecast to become a 
remnant low in a couple of days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Olana Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sun Oct 25 2026 
257 
WTPA43 PHFO 260232
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Storm Olana Discussion Number   3
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP032026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Sun Oct 25 2026

There have not been any significant changes with Olana over the
past several hours. The storm continues to produce a relatively
concentrated area of deep convection near and to the northeast of
the center and in a broken band well southeast of the center. The
storm has a sheared and ragged appearance in satellite images,
likely due to the influence of an approaching mid- to upper-level
trough. The initial intensity is held at 35 kt, based on the
various objective and subjective satellite estimates.
 
Olana could strengthen a little in the short term, but a notable
increase in southwesterly vertical wind shear and intrusions of dry
air should cause weakening to begin on Monday. Given the expected
hostile conditions and latest model guidance, Olana is now expected
to become a remnant low by 48 hours and degenerate into an
elongated trough by midweek. This forecast lies near the high end
of the model guidance in the short term, but then falls in line
with the bulk of the models after that.
 
The storm is moving east-northeastward at about 8 kt. The models
show Olana generally tracking eastward over the next few days, but
in an erratic fashion as it moves along the base of a broad
deep-layer trough. The NHC track forecast is similar to the previous
one and is based on a blend of the HCCA and TVCA consensus aids.
Based on the latest forecast, Olana should dissipate before it
reaches Johnston Atoll.
